subject: Adding spline function from mgcv package to ggplot2

messages.author: 1382389258fcbbc7
messages.subject: Adding spline function from mgcv package to ggplot2
parts:
Hi and thank you for an absolutely brilliant package!

I have a question regardig a gam in the mgcv-package. I would like to plot the predicted function on my raw data. I found this site, but for some reason I am not able to duplicate what has been done:
http://www.ats.ucla.edu/stat/r/faq/smooths.htm

# Some dummy data:
mydata<- data.frame(factor1 = factor(rep(LETTERS[1:6], each = 80)), #Dummy data
                    factor2 = factor(rep(c(1:2), each = 16)),
                    var1 = rnorm(120, mean = rep(c(0, 3, 15), each = 40),
                                 sd = rep(c(1, 3, 6), each = 20)),
                    var2 = rnorm(120, mean = rep(c(0.1, 0.023, 0.05), each = 40),
                                 sd = rep(c(2, 4, 7), each = 20)))

library(ggplot2)
library(mgcv)

#My model:
Mod <- gam(var1 ~ s(var2, k=4), data= mydata)

# My plot
p <- ggplot(mydata, aes(x = var2, y = var1)) +
  geom_point()+
  ylab(expression('Heterocyst frequency  ' * 
                    group("", "(mm"*" fil)"^{-1}, "")))+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(strip.background = element_blank()) +
  facet_grid(.~factor2)
p

#Does not work:
p + stat_smooth(method = "gam", formula = var1 ~ s(var2, k=4), size = 1)

p + stat_smooth(method="gam") # why does this look linear?  
p + stat_smooth() #The loess smooth - I want the spline function from mgcv

I really need some help. Thank you for taking your time!
with kind regards
Anna Zakrisson

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Adding spline function from mgcv package to ggplot2
parts:
You want

p + stat_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, k=4), size = 1)

The formula in stat_smooth() is always of the form y ~ f(x) for some
suitable function f; in this case, f(x) = s(x, k = 4).

Dennis
